# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 7 | **Condition:** Better preserved

---

**7:1** I thank You, O Lord, for You have made me a source of streams in a dry land, a spring of water in a parched land.

**7:2** And an irrigation for a garden [...] a pool and a living spring.

**7:3** And You have set a planting of cypress and elm together with cedar for Your glory.

**7:4** Trees of life beside a hidden spring, concealed among all the trees by the water.

**7:5** They shall put forth a shoot for an everlasting planting, taking root before they blossom.

**7:6** And they shall stretch out their roots to the watercourse and its trunk shall lie open to the living water.

**7:7** And it shall become an eternal fountain. And on the shoots of its foliage all the beasts of the forest shall feed.

**7:8** And its trunk shall be trodden by all who pass along the way, and its boughs by every bird.

**7:9** And all the trees by the water shall tower above it, for in their planting they grow tall.

**7:10** But they send not their root to the watercourse.

**7:11** And the shoot of the holy planting, the planting of truth, is hidden, without esteem, and the mystery of its seal is unknown.

**7:12** And You, O God, have guarded its fruit by the mystery of mighty warriors and spirits of holiness.

**7:13** And the whirling flame of fire, that no stranger may enter the fountain of life.

**7:14** Nor drink of the holy waters with the everlasting trees.

**7:15** Nor bear his fruit with the planting of the clouds, for he sees without recognizing.

**7:16** And he considers without believing in the source of life. And he sends forth the bud of [...] the eternal fountain.

**7:17** And I have become the scorn of flooding rivers, for they cast their mire upon me.

**7:18** But You, O my God, have placed in my mouth the early rain for all [...] and a spring of living water.

**7:19** And it shall not fail, opening the heavens without ceasing. And they shall become a torrent overflowing.

**7:20** To the boundless seas [...] and they shall burst forth suddenly from concealment, and they shall become [...] waters in abundance.

**7:21** For it was hidden from the eyes of all [...] and veiled from mortal sight.

**7:22** And they were counted by Israel as worthless [...] and among the trees by the water.

**7:23** But the fruitful planting [...] shall put forth its branch for an everlasting planting.

**7:24** And it shall take root throughout the earth, and by its branches all [...] trees by the water.

**7:25** And they shall spread out their roots into the dry land and [...] shall stream forth.

**7:26** For it is a planting of truth that brings forth branches of holiness for an everlasting planting.

**7:27** And all the rivers of Eden shall water its holy boughs.

**7:28** And it shall become a mighty tree with vast branches, and all the beasts of the field shall shelter in it.

**7:29** And its shade shall cover the whole earth, and its crown shall reach to the clouds.

**7:30** And its roots shall descend to the abyss.

**7:31** They shall put forth a shoot for an everlasting planting, taking root before they blossom.

**7:32** And they shall stretch out their roots to the watercourse.

**7:33** And the fountain shall be opened for a blessed planting, an eternal wellspring.

**7:34** And all the beasts of the forest shall feed on its leafy boughs.

**7:35** And its trunk shall be trodden by all who pass over, and its branches shall sustain every bird.

**7:36** And all the trees by the water shall not prevail against it, for the root of its planting reaches to the watercourse.

**7:37** And it yields its fruit in its season and its leaf does not wither.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Column 7 consensus is primarily LOGOS-based with EMET corrections. Key decisions: "spring of water" (EMET, 7:1) over "fountain"; "hidden spring" (LOGOS, 7:4); "trees by the water" (LOGOS) consistently; "whirling flame" (LOGOS, 7:13); "stranger" (EMET, 7:13); "shelter" (LOGOS, 7:28). Final verse (7:37) echoes Psalm 1:3.*
